_comment: The registry: which repos exist in this tree, and which tracks each one loads. Copy to registry.json — deploy.py does that for you on a fresh clone — and then let `/grove:register-project` fill it in from inside each repo, rather than writing entries by hand.
_what_grove_reads: Grove itself reads three things and nothing else: `projects` (where each repo is, and its tracks), `ignored` (repos deliberately left off, so the offer stops coming back), and `keys_root`. Everything else here is read by whoever put it there.
_extensions: A marketplace layered on grove keeps its own facts in this same file, because a repo has one identity and splitting it across two registries is how two answers drift apart. `apps` below is exactly that: an app's store identifiers belong to the marketplace that ships apps, and grove treats those entries as repos like any other — it reads `repo` and `tracks`, and has no opinion about `platforms` or anything else in them. If you ship nothing, delete the `apps` section; nothing here needs it.
_keys_root_note: Where credentials live, relative to the tree's base — never inside a repo. A skill says $KEYS_ROOT and never names this folder, so renaming it is a one-line change here. KEYS_ROOT in the environment wins, for a vault outside the tree. Grove has no secrets of its own; this exists so that a skill which does can name one portably.
_roots_note: Roots are RELATIVE to the tree's base. That is what lets the same file work on another machine: the registry says how the tree is SHAPED, the machine says where it sits. An absolute path is honoured too, for a repo that genuinely lives elsewhere.
_base_note: Where the tree sits. Omit it and the base is the directory holding grove itself, which is right when you cloned grove beside your repos. Set it — an absolute path, or ~/something — when grove lives somewhere else, which is the normal case if you added it as a marketplace rather than cloning it into your work tree. GROVE_DEV_ROOT in the environment wins over both.
_tracks_note: Track names are plugin names, from any marketplace you have installed. Grove writes only the tracks it ships itself and reports the rest — a name it does not recognise is another marketplace's business, not an error.

_example_data.role: the shared data several repos read
_example_data._note: Every registry name becomes an anchor: this one is reachable as $EXAMPLE_DATA in any session on this machine.

_example_site._site_note: Marks this repo as the website — it becomes $SITE. Optional: having no website is a normal case.

apps._comment: An EXTENSION section — see `_extensions` above. Grove reads `repo` and `tracks` from each entry, so an app repo is guarded and reported like any other place; the rest of the entry belongs to the marketplace that ships apps.

ignored._comment: Repos deliberately NOT registered. Listed only so the offer stops coming back — an unanswered offer that returns every session trains you to ignore it, which is how a prompt stops working. Removing an entry here makes the offer come back.
